name: MiniZero
description: This paper presents MiniZero, a zero-knowledge learning framework that supports four state-of-the-art algorithms, including AlphaZero, MuZero, Gumbel AlphaZero, and Gumbel MuZero. While these algorithms have demonstrated super-human performance in many games, it remains unclear which among them is most suitable or efficient for specific tasks. Through MiniZero, we systematically evaluate the performance of each algorithm in two board games, 9x9 Go and 8x8 Othello, as well as 57 Atari games. For two board games, using more simulations generally results in higher performance. However, the choice of AlphaZero and MuZero may differ based on game properties. For Atari games, both MuZero and Gumbel MuZero are worth considering. Since each game has unique characteristics, different algorithms and simulations yield varying results. typical_sota_score: Win rate up to ~95–100% on small board games (9x9 Go, 8x8 Othello) for strong AlphaZero/MuZero variants; Atari normalized scores vary greatly by game (from near 0 to well above human baseline depending on the title).
reputation: A research benchmark used to compare zero-knowledge RL algorithms across board games and Atari environments.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; scores are environment-specific and not directly comparable across games, with strong dependence on simulation budget and training compute.
